peer_results.rationale: The provided AMD disclosures discuss the overall income tax provision and effective rate drivers (pre-tax income, intercompany transactions) or gaming segment performance, but do not contain specific comparable text regarding the mechanics, risks, or quantified benefits of tax holidays or incentives as presented in the target AVGO disclosure.

comparisons.peer_topic: Factors impacting effective tax rate and variability
comparisons.peer_summary: Changes in the volume and mix of profits, business operating models, tax audits, deferred tax valuations, non-deductible expenses, tax credits, tax holidays, tax laws (including OECD Pillar Two), accounting standards, and repatriation decisions can impact the effective tax rate and cash payments. These factors may cause significant variability in financial results.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and INTC discuss the risk and uncertainty surrounding tax holidays and incentives in their fiscal year 2024 Item 7 disclosures. AVGO explicitly warns that its interpretations of tax incentives are not binding on taxing authorities and that incorrect assumptions could adversely affect benefits (referencing Singapore and Malaysia incentives in year-over-year context). Similarly, INTC lists 'expirations or changes in our ability to secure new tax holidays and incentives' as a specific factor that can impact its effective tax rate and cause variability in financial results. While AVGO quantifies the benefit reduction and warns of adverse effects from incorrect assumptions, INTC broadly categorizes the availability and expiration of these incentives as a driver of rate variability.

sentences.text: Our interpretations and conclusions regarding the tax incentives are not binding on any taxing authority, and if our assumptions about tax and other laws are incorrect, the benefits of the tax incentives may be adversely affected.
▪expirations or changes in our ability to secure new tax holidays and incentives;

comparisons.peer_summary: Tax incentive arrangements in jurisdictions like Singapore expire through 2034 and require meeting business and employment thresholds. Due to low profitability and the mix of income, these incentives were not material in 2024 or 2023, but they reduced the tax provision by $1.12 billion in 2022.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and MU disclose the financial impact of tax incentive arrangements on their income tax provisions. AVGO states that tax incentives and holidays decreased its provision by approximately $2,261 million in fiscal 2024. MU discusses its tax incentive arrangements in jurisdictions like Singapore, noting that while they reduced the tax provision by $1.12 billion in 2022, the benefit was not material in 2024 or 2023 due to low profitability and income mix. Both companies explicitly link their tax incentive benefits to specific jurisdictions and compliance conditions.

sentences.text: Before taking into consideration the effects of the U.S. Tax Cuts and Jobs Act and other indirect tax impacts, the effect of these tax incentives and tax holiday decreased the provision for income taxes by approximately $2,261 million and $2,104 million for fiscal years 2024 and 2023, respectively.
The effect of tax incentive arrangements reduced our tax provision by $1.12 billion (benefiting our diluted earnings per share by $1.00) for 2022.
